desc:
Extension popup and side panel design from Ecom Swift LLC builds the popups, side panels and options pages of your extension so each one opens quickly, fits its space in the browser and connects to your existing logic.

## How do a popup, a side panel and an options page differ?

A popup is a small window that opens when the user clicks the toolbar icon and closes the moment they click elsewhere. A side panel is a taller panel docked beside the page that can stay open while the user browses. An options page is a full tab where settings live. Each one has its own size, lifespan and purpose.

Treating them as the same thing is the most common mistake. A form that suits an options tab feels cramped in a popup, and a popup layout looks empty when stretched across a side panel.

## Why each surface needs its own layout

A popup has limited width and height, and it is destroyed whenever it loses focus. Anything the user typed, or any list they scrolled, is gone unless the extension saved it. A side panel stays open, so it must keep up with changes on the current page. An options page can hold longer explanations and many controls, so it needs structure.

When these surfaces are designed together, they feel like one product. The same colors, buttons and wording appear everywhere, and a setting changed in one place shows up in the others. Users stop wondering where to click.

## What well-built extension surfaces include

- A popup sized to its content, with scrolling only where the content needs it.
- A side panel that opens from the toolbar icon and responds to page changes.
- An options page with grouped settings and clear labels.
- Shared components, so buttons and inputs look the same in all three.
- State saved between opens, so work is not lost when a popup closes.
- Settings synced across surfaces, so a change is reflected everywhere.
- Loading and error states that tell people what is happening.
- Controls reachable by keyboard, with a visible focus mark.
- Light and dark themes that follow the user's preference.
- Wiring to your background worker and content scripts through messages.

## How we build the screens

We start with a short review of what each surface needs to do. For each one we decide the size, the content and the actions, and we confirm that plan with you. Then we build the screens, connect them to your existing code and test each in Chrome and Edge, including quick open and close, small windows and long content.

Our packages scale with the number of surfaces. Basic delivers one well-fitted popup or options page. Standard builds a popup and a side panel that share one style, with the panel opening from the toolbar icon and state saved between opens. Premium delivers all three surfaces as a connected set, with up to five views, synced settings, loading and error states and an accessibility pass on contrast and focus.

We use plain web technologies unless your project already uses a framework, and we follow what you have.

## Do and avoid with extension screens

**Do:**
- Put the most common action at the top.
- Save form input as the user types.
- Design for the smallest size first.
- Keep labels short and place them near their controls.
- Test with the browser's own zoom set to a larger size.

**Avoid:**
- Filling a popup with settings that belong on the options page.
- Letting the side panel reload and lose its position.
- Using hover as the only way to reveal a control.
- Adding a framework for a single small screen.
- Forgetting the empty state for a new user.

## Who this is for

It suits an extension owner whose popup has outgrown its space. It suits a team adding a side panel to a research or writing tool. And it suits a founder who has working logic but only a rough interface and needs polished screens attached to it.

## What we need from you

Send the extension code, or the logic and a description if the screens are new. Tell us which actions each surface must offer and share any brand colors. Mention any browsers you must support, since side panel support differs between browsers.

We never ask for passwords. A repository invite or a zip file is enough. After you order, we reply with a short layout plan for each surface before we build.
